findings.title: website_name bypasses TL0 anonymous website redaction
findings.body: website, location, and bio are omitted for trust-level 0 users viewed anonymously via untrusted_attributes (include_<attr>? returns false when scope.restrict_user_fields? is true). website_name is derived from that same website value and is not in that list. The new include_website_name method is also never called: ActiveModel Serializers only invokes include_website_name? (every other hook in this file uses the question-mark form), so the attribute is always serialized. Even renaming the method would not close the hole, because it only checks website.present? and does not apply restrict_user_fields?. The profile template now renders the link from model.website_name instead of a client-side name computed from model.website. Previously the omitted website made that label empty and the link stayed hidden; anonymous visitors will now see the TL0 user's website host and, when the domain check matches, the path. Gate website_name with the same untrusted-attribute rule and cover it in the existing anonymous TL0 serializer spec with a website actually set.

findings.title: Same-domain label check is case-sensitive, drops port, and mismatches subdomains
findings.body: Whether to append the path is decided by case-sensitive equality of URI#host and Discourse.current_hostname, plus a case-sensitive ends_with? / dot-label split. Hosts are case-insensitive, so http://Example.com/docs on an example.com instance fails the match and the path this change is meant to show is dropped. URI#host also strips the port, unlike the removed client logic (website.split("/")[2] kept example.com:8080). A non-default port is therefore labeled example.com or example.com/admin while the href is still http://example.com:8080/..., so the link looks like the forum origin. Matching is asymmetric: forums.example.com shows the path for a website on parent example.com, but example.com does not show the path for https://www.example.com/docs or https://blog.example.com/docs, because those hosts are longer and are not a suffix of the instance host. The else branch's ends_with?("." + website_host) also treats any string suffix as the same site, so a website host of com or co.uk matches ordinary forum hostnames and gets its path appended. Compare downcased hosts, keep a non-default port in the label, and only treat equal hosts or a real parent/child relationship in both directions as the same site.

findings.title: URI parse failure hides the website link entirely
findings.body: website_name does URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil and returns nil when parsing fails. The profile template only shows the globe link when model.website_name is present, so a parse failure removes the website from the profile even though model.website is still set. Ruby's URI parser rejects non-ASCII IRIs and unescaped characters, including realistic values such as http://example.com/ü or a URL with a space in the path. The old client label used split("/")[2] and still displayed the host for those strings. Falling back to a host-only label (or an IDN-aware parser) is needed so a path the strict parser rejects does not drop the whole website.
